messages.subject: Variance-covariance and Delta Method
parts:
Hello, 

I am interested in applying the delta method to inla models to obtain proper estimates with standard errors for offset parameters between categorical predictors. To do this I need the variance-covariance matrix for the model, which I do not see in the model output object. What is the best way to extract the var-covar matrix from an INLA model, or is there a better way to get proper estimates with standard error (rather than offset estimates) with INLA model objects? 

Thanks! 

Ben

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Variance-covariance and Delta Method
parts:
Hi,

Where you say “standard error”, I assume you mean “posterior standard deviation (or variance)”?
I can see at least two options:
1. Use the lincomb feature to specify linear combinations of the latent variables that you want to estimate.
2. Use posterior sampling with inla.posterior.sample. With this method you can compute Monte Carlo estimates of any functional of the model components.

Finn
